text:
alex: Heads up — I'm standing up a temporary compat-lock on runtime v3.2 for EU canary. Nightly infra tests showed an SDK->runtime signature mismatch on long-sequence requests. Putting it in hold while we triage.

deploy-bot: created hold 'compat-lock-178001' (scope: runtime:v3.2, region: eu-west, affected: canary). Reason: sdk-client 2.8 produced KV cache misalignment on seq>8192. Initiated at 1780012345.

maria: Thanks Alex. Can you paste the failing trace? Is this regress or flaky infra?

alex: quick snippet from the failing job: ```
ERROR RuntimeMismatch: KVCacheSequenceOverflow at runtime/kernel_cache.cpp:412
Request: model=llama3q-v2 seq_len=9216 sdk-client=2.8
Stack: ...
```

sam: Oof. If it's strictly long-seq we could route long requests to runtime v3.1 for the canary cohort and keep v3.2 for short seq. Can deploy-bot do per-route routing?

deploy-bot: routing change possible. Suggested command: `/deploy route-update --route canary-eu --fallback runtime:v3.1 --match "len>8192"` (dry-run available).

anya: Before any routing flip, can we run a focused repro on a dedicated canary node? If it's a quant/kernel edgecase we should capture heap + kernel logs. I can spin one up and run the failing payloads.

alex: yes please @anya — repro on a pinned canary node would be ideal. Also putting a short checklist:
- repro on pinned node (anya)
- run SDK 2.7 vs 2.8 diff (maria)
- eval alert thresholds (latency/error rate) for routing decision (sam)
- decide unhold criteria (engineering + SRE)

maria: I'll diff the SDK changes; early glance shows a small KV cache header change in 2.8 that could change alignment. If confirmed, we can ship a tiny shim in sdk-client to maintain backwards alignment.

sam: For immediate mitigation, I'm +1 on routing long seq to v3.1 for canary. That buys time with minimal rollback surface. If we do that, let's annotate the change in release-notes and the console so customers on dedicated tiers are aware.

deploy-bot: scheduled a routing dry-run for 1780012600; will execute only after approval. Current hold prevents runtime:v3.2 from receiving new canary long-seq traffic.

anya: Repro started on node eu-canary-03. Uploading heap + kvdump link when done. Also will enable verbose kernel logs (`KV_CACHE_DEBUG=1`).

alex: thanks. If the repro confirms kernel-side off-by-one we should escalate to runtime-owners and consider a micro-patch. If it's SDK-only, prefer a shim. Either way, don't lift the hold until we have a validated fix.

maria: diff shows header field reordering in 2.8 that could explain the alignment shift. Running a quick local with SDK 2.7 -> 2.8 toggles now.

sam: tagging @oncall-sre just in case latency spikes. We should have a rollback plan if routing introduces unexpected downstream regressions.

oncall-sre: I'm watching. If the dry-run routes more than 10% traffic or latency >2x baseline, abort and rollback to original routing.

deploy-bot: dry-run results (1780012600): routing decisions validated, estimated impact <3% traffic shift, latency delta within SLA. Awaiting explicit approval to promote.

alex: Approve routing promotion to reroute len>8192 -> runtime:v3.1 for canary. Keep hold on v3.2 until either kernel patch or sdk shim validated.

maria: I'll prepare the shim PR and a unit test that reproduces the header case. Linking when ready.

anya: repro confirmed: same exception + kvdump shows misaligned offsets. Kernel-level off-by-one in `apply_kv_header()` suspected. Sending dump and verbose logs: https://artifacts.internal/runs/178001/kvdump.tar.gz

sam: Good catch. After shim or kernel fix, what's our unhold criteria? Suggest: 1) all canary repro tests pass on v3.2, 2) 24h stable canary metrics (error rate <0.05%), 3) release note + rollout plan documented.

alex: Agree on those unhold criteria. Add an explicit rollback plan: if anything exceeds thresholds, route back to previous routing and re-enable hold.

deploy-bot: noted. hold 'compat-lock-178001' remains active. Will auto-expire only with a manual `release-hold compat-lock-178001 --by <owner>` command.

maria: PR opened: `sdk-client#498` — adds shim to restore legacy header ordering. CI includes targeted failing-case. PTAL: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-client/pull/498

anya: After applying shim in canary, I'll re-run repro on eu-canary-03. If green, we can run small canary promotion tests.

alex: Great — let's keep notifications here. If anyone wants to override or propose a full rollback of runtime v3.2, post your reasoning and we'll convene a quick triage. For now, routing mitigation + shim seems lowest-risk. :thumbsup:

sam: Recording for release notes: runtime v3.2 temporarily isolation for long-seq requests in EU due to SDK alignment change; mitigated by routing and SDK shim. Will draft a short blurb once we validate.

deploy-bot: hold 'compat-lock-178001' status check at 1780012920: active, owners=[alex,maria], scope=runtime:v3.2 (eu-west canary).
